business_process: 911 call intake, emergency medical dispatch, and dispatch (County A)
description: Receive County A CAD-to-CAD incidents and transferred medical callers; run the emergency medical dispatch protocol; assign and track the closest unit
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A delayed ambulance can contribute to death or disability; exclusive 911 provider for about 520,000 residents; manual mode is judged safe for about 2 hours before unit tracking errors grow; CAD database point-in-time restore supports a 15-minute RPO
manual_workaround: Manual dispatch binder: paper incident cards, unit status board, run cards by zone; County A PSAP voice-announces new calls on the P25 system; after 2 hours ask County A to send overflow calls to the mutual-aid provider
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-06; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-10; SYS-11
dependent_third_parties: County A PSAP and county CAD; county P25 radio system; hosted phone vendor; cloud provider; CAD vendor; ISPs
dependent_people_or_facilities: Telecommunicators and supervisors; primary communications center; backup center at Station 10
quantified_operational_impact: About 320 County A 911 responses a day (about 27 in a 2-hour window); manual mode needs 2 extra telecommunicators per shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: County A agreement: notice of any dispatch system outage longer than 15 minutes; response-time standards measured monthly
patient_safety_impact: Severe: delayed response to cardiac arrest, stroke, trauma, or obstetric calls
county_agreement_linkage: County A agreement sections on response-time standards, communications center continuity plan, and outage notice (section 7 of the facts file)

business_process: 911 dispatch for the County B zones (CAD-to-CAD)
description: Receive County B incidents for the 2 company zones over CAD-to-CAD; assign and track units
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same safety driver as BP-01 for about 210,000 residents; County B does not transfer callers, so call information arrives only by CAD-to-CAD or voice
manual_workaround: County B communications center voice-announces calls in the company zones on the county P25 talkgroup; paper incident cards
dependent_third_parties: County B communications center and county CAD; county P25 radio system; cloud provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Telecommunicators; primary and backup communications centers
quantified_operational_impact: About 90 County B responses a day (about 8 in a 2-hour window)
quantified_regulatory_impact: County B zone agreement: monthly response-time report
patient_safety_impact: Severe: delayed response to time-critical calls
county_agreement_linkage: County B zone agreement: monthly reporting and security incident notice (section 7)

business_process: Field communications, unit tracking, and station alerting
description: AVL positions for unit recommendation, mobile data to MDCs, radio, and station alerting (tones and bay doors)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without AVL the closest unit cannot be chosen; radio is the life-safety channel and is county-operated; station alerting failure slows turnout; AVL history is needed only for reports (daily backup)
manual_workaround: Crews report location and status by radio; supervisors alert stations by phone and radio; county P25 radio in every vehicle
dependent_third_parties: County P25 radio systems; cellular carriers; station alerting vendor
quantified_operational_impact: 92 ambulances and 14 support vehicles; turnout time rises by about 1 minute per call without station alerting
quantified_regulatory_impact: Response-time standards in both county agreements
patient_safety_impact: Severe: wrong or slower unit assigned to time-critical calls
county_agreement_linkage: Response-time standards in both county agreements

business_process: Interfacility and non-emergency transport scheduling and dispatch
description: Book trips from hospitals and nursing facilities; schedule BLS, ALS, and CCT units; dispatch and track
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $112,000 of revenue a day; delayed hospital discharges and critical care transfers; facilities move work to competitors after repeated delays
manual_workaround: Paper trip log; facilities call the supervisor cell line; defer scheduled non-urgent trips; CCT requests handled first
dependent_third_parties: Hospitals and nursing facilities; hosted phone vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 178 trips a day; about 59 trips in 8 hours, with about 40% of the revenue on deferred trips not recovered
quantified_regulatory_impact: Facility contract service levels (pickup within agreed windows)

business_process: Patient care documentation and hospital record delivery
description: Crews document care on ePCR tablets; records are delivered to the receiving hospital and exported to the state
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The receiving hospital must be able to get the patient care record on request within 48 hours of dispatch (Rule 64J-1.014, F.A.C.); tablets store records offline; verbal report at handoff covers immediate care
manual_workaround: Paper patient care records in downtime kits; back-enter into the ePCR within 48 hours
dependent_people_or_facilities: Field clinicians; Director of Clinical Services
quantified_operational_impact: About 410 records a day; back-entry takes about 20 minutes per record
quantified_regulatory_impact: 48-hour hospital record rule (Rule 64J-1.014, F.A.C.); accurate records (Fla. Stat. 401.30(1))
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: hospital lacks prehospital details if the verbal report is incomplete

description: Cardiac monitors send 12-lead ECGs to receiving hospitals through the monitor vendor's cloud relay for heart attack and stroke pre-alerts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hospital activation of the catheterization lab depends on early ECG review; crews can describe findings by phone or radio
manual_workaround: Crews phone the receiving emergency department and read the monitor interpretation and key findings; personal phones and messaging apps are not used to send ECG images
dependent_third_parties: Cardiac monitor relay vendor; cellular carriers; receiving hospitals
patient_safety_impact: Severe: delayed treatment of heart attack patients if pre-alerts fail

business_process: System status management and unit posting
description: Plan coverage by hour and area; move idle units to posting locations using the CAD posting module and the forecasting model (AI-004)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Coverage gaps raise response times within hours; posting plans can be run from printed plans; history is needed only for the forecast model
manual_workaround: Printed hourly posting plan by day of week; supervisors move units by radio
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-06 (data and reporting account); AI-004
quantified_operational_impact: Response-time compliance falls about 3 points per shift without dynamic posting (estimate from the 2025 CAD upgrade outage)
quantified_regulatory_impact: County A liquidated damages apply if monthly compliance falls below 90%
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: longer responses in uncovered areas

description: Import trips from the ePCR; code level of service and mileage; submit claims; post payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash flow: about $1.87 million of collections a week (about $373,000 per business day); payers accept late claims within filing limits
manual_workaround: Queue trips; submit high-dollar claims through payer portals; draw on the credit line
quantified_regulatory_impact: Medicare and Medicaid timely filing limits; certification statements on file (42 CFR 410.40(e))

business_process: Billing services for municipal fire-rescue clients
description: Import client ePCR exports; code; submit claims; post payments; report to each client
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $1.0 million of client collections a week (about $200,000 per business day); client contracts set claim submission service levels; client trust drives renewals
manual_workaround: Queue client claims; daily status calls with each client; payer portals for high-dollar claims
dependent_third_parties: Billing platform vendor; clearinghouse; client ePCR vendors
dependent_people_or_facilities: Billing services staff (part of the 48 revenue cycle staff)
quantified_operational_impact: About 270 client claims a business day for 4 clients
quantified_regulatory_impact: Client BAAs and service agreements (company is a business associate)

description: Receive physician certification statements and facility face sheets by cloud fax; attach to the billing record
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Medicare requires certification statements on file for non-emergency transports (42 CFR 410.40(e)); missing statements delay or deny claims
manual_workaround: Facilities hand paper PCS to crews at pickup; scan later
dependent_third_parties: Productivity suite vendor; cloud fax vendor

business_process: Crew scheduling, timekeeping, and credential tracking
description: Shift schedules for 420 clinicians and 52 communications staff; time capture; EMT, paramedic, and critical care certification tracking
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Ambulances cannot be staffed without the schedule beyond the printed 2-week copy; staffing with an expired certification is a licensure issue
manual_workaround: Printed 2-week schedule; supervisors fill open shifts by phone; manual certification list exported weekly
quantified_regulatory_impact: Staffing only certified clinicians (Chapter 401, Florida Statutes)
county_agreement_linkage: Unit-hour commitments in the County A agreement

description: Payroll for 600 employees; onboarding and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; late pay affects retention of scarce paramedics
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the payroll provider; manual adjustments later
quantified_operational_impact: About $1.6 million gross payroll every 2 weeks
quantified_regulatory_impact: State and federal wage payment rules

business_process: County performance reporting and state data reporting
description: Monthly response-time reports to both counties; EMSTARS submissions to the state
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: County reports are monthly; state data can be submitted late with notice; data comes from CAD and ePCR backups
manual_workaround: Submit late with an explanation; rebuild reports from restored data
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-06 (data and reporting account)
dependent_third_parties: State EMS office; County A and County B
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of Government Contracts; Director of Clinical Services
quantified_operational_impact: 2 county reports a month; daily state exports
quantified_regulatory_impact: Rule 64J-1.014, F.A.C. (data reporting); county reporting clauses
county_agreement_linkage: Monthly reporting clauses in both county agreements

description: Preventive maintenance, vehicle readiness checks, and medical supply restocking for 106 vehicles
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Vehicles keep running for days on existing schedules; paper checklists exist
manual_workaround: Paper readiness checklists; manual supply requests
dependent_third_parties: Fleet maintenance SaaS vendor; parts and supply vendors
quantified_operational_impact: About 15 vehicles in scheduled maintenance a week
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: a vehicle with a missed safety check stays in service
county_agreement_linkage: Fleet readiness reporting in the County A agreement

business_process: Clinical quality review and protocol management
description: Medical Director review of high-risk calls; protocol updates pushed to ePCR and CAD
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reviews can wait a week; protocols in force stay on tablets
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: delayed feedback on unsafe practice
